4. Halaku Khan sacked Baghdad in:
(A) 1254 AD (B) 1256 AD
(C) 1258 AD (D) None of these
Associated Information:
Halaku Khan, also known as Hulegu, sacked Baghdad in
1258. This was a devastating event that marked the end
of the Islamic Golden Age and had significant
repercussions for the region.
Halaku Khan was
- Mongol Emperor: Hulagu was a grandson of Genghis
Khan and the brother of Kublai Khan.
i Conquests: He conquered vast territories, including
“"odern-day Iran, Iraq, and parts of Turkiye.
- Founder of the Ilkhanate: Hulagu established the
lIkhanate dynasty in Persia (modern-day Iran), which
lasted from 1256 to 1335.
The Siege of Baghdad
- The Siege: Hulegu led a massive army of over 138,000
men to Baghdad in 1258.

the Caliph, Hulegu's army attacked and breached the
